App.CloseDialog.Both.PrimaryButton: Write the change, stop the download and close
App.CloseDialog.Both.Title: A download is running and one change is not written
App.CloseDialog.Content: Bannerlord or its launcher is running, so the last change to your load order has not reached LauncherData.xml.
App.CloseDialog.Download.Content: Closing BEM stops the download it is running. Everything already transferred stays on your disk, and Unfinished Downloads on the Versions page carries on from there rather than starting again.
App.CloseDialog.Download.Title: A Download Is Still Running
App.CloseDialog.Title: One Change Not Written Yet
BootChecks.AcceptRiskButton.Tooltip: Stops this exact finding from counting against the Health badge again until its wording changes. It stays listed here, marked accepted.
BootChecks.AutoBisectionButton.Tooltip: Only for a crash that happens while the game is starting, and only once a boot check has actually failed.
BootChecks.BisectionSection.Blurb: Everything else in Diagnostics ranks suspects from evidence that was already on disk. This turns mods off and on and watches the crash come and go, which is the only thing that earns the word caused. It starts with three runs of your load order exactly as it is, and refuses outright if the crash does not reproduce at least twice in three.
BootChecks.BisectionSection.Tooltip: Turns mods off and on across repeated runs until the crash moves with one of them.
BootChecks.Blurb: What starting the game actually did, and the experiment that finds the mod when the evidence on disk will not.
BootChecks.BootCheckSection.Tooltip: Starts the game with your current load order and closes it again at the first frame.
BootChecks.CancelDryRunButton.Tooltip: Kills the game process and puts your LauncherData.xml and Configs back.
BootChecks.CheckBootsButton.Tooltip: Starts the game with this exact load order, watches every module load, and closes it again at the first frame. Takes a minute or two. Your LauncherData.xml and Configs are copied first and put back afterwards, and the load order itself is never written. If a file cannot be copied, the result names it rather than claiming it was protected.
BootChecks.ClearScopeButton.Tooltip: Unticks everything and forgets what you recorded against it.
BootChecks.CopyBackupPathMenuItem: Copy the load order backup path
BootChecks.CopyBackupPathMenuItem.Toolti: Copies the path to the load order saved before this search started.
BootChecks.CopyFailingModulesMenuItem: Copy the modules still under test
BootChecks.CopyFailingModulesMenuItem.To: Copies one module id per line.
BootChecks.CopyScopeButton.Tooltip: Copies one module id per line.
BootChecks.CopySessionRowMenuItem.Toolti: Copies the two lines this row shows.
BootChecks.DeleteSessionButton.Tooltip: Deletes the saved session only; it touches no mod and no load order.
BootChecks.FinishedRunButton.Tooltip: BEM looks for a matching new crash report first, and only asks you when it cannot tell.
BootChecks.FirstChanceSection: Exceptions that were thrown and handled
BootChecks.FirstChanceSection.Blurb: An exception something caught and swallowed leaves no crash report, but it can leave state broken enough that something innocent falls over minutes later. These are leads, never a reason the game stopped.
BootChecks.FirstChanceSection.Tooltip: Faults something caught and swallowed, which are leads rather than causes.
BootChecks.ForgetObservationButton.Toolt: Removes the selected record, so the search will ask for that run itself.
BootChecks.GuidedBisectionButton.Tooltip: For anything that needs gameplay to reproduce, with your load order put back after every run.
BootChecks.InScopeCheckBox.Tooltip: In the scope: the search is allowed to turn this one off.
BootChecks.LastBootCheckSection: What the last boot check found
BootChecks.LastBootCheckSection.Tooltip: The result of the last dry run, started above.
BootChecks.LaunchRunButton.Tooltip: Starts the game on exactly the configuration named above, and your own load order goes back the moment you answer.
BootChecks.ListModsButton.Tooltip: Reads your load order again and keeps whatever you had already ticked.
BootChecks.NoInformationButton.Tooltip: Counts the run as no information and offers the same configuration again rather than reading it as clean.
BootChecks.ObservationsHeading.Blurb: Tick the second box on every mod in the scope that was on for a run you have already done, then say what that run did. BEM will use the answer instead of asking you to run it again. Get one of these wrong and the search follows it into the wrong half, so read the line below before you press either button.
BootChecks.ObservationsHeading.Tooltip: Outcomes you already know, so the search does not spend a launch asking again.
BootChecks.RecordCrashedButton.Tooltip: Records the configuration described above as one that reproduces the crash.
BootChecks.RecordDidNotCrashButton.Toolt: Records the configuration described above as clean.
BootChecks.ReportCrashedButton.Tooltip: Records this configuration as one that reproduces the crash.
BootChecks.ReproductionStepBox.Header: What you do to make it happen
BootChecks.ReproductionStepBox.Placehold: start a new campaign and reach the culture stage
BootChecks.ReproductionStepBox.Tooltip: Repeated back to you word for word in every run's instruction, so you are always doing the same thing.
BootChecks.RereadRunsButton.Tooltip: Reads the copies again; it writes to none of them and deletes none of them.
BootChecks.RereadTraceButton.Tooltip: Reads the newest trace on disk again, without re-scanning the crash folders.
BootChecks.ResumeSessionButton.Tooltip: Continues from the run it left off on, against your load order as it is now.
BootChecks.RunsCapturedSection.Tooltip: What your recent runs wrote, read out of BEM's own copies.
BootChecks.ScopeExpander.Blurb: Tick the mods the crash is already known to be inside. Everything you do not tick stays on for every single run, so the search never asks a question about it. Leave all of them unticked to search the whole load order.
BootChecks.ScopeExpander.Header: Search only inside mods I choose
BootChecks.ScopeExpander.Tooltip: Confines the search to mods you choose, instead of your whole load order.
BootChecks.ScopeFilterBox.Placeholder: part of a name or a module id
BootChecks.ScopeFilterBox.Tooltip: Narrows the list below; anything already in the scope stays visible.
BootChecks.SessionsHeading: Searches you can pick up again
BootChecks.SessionsHeading.Tooltip: Saved sessions, each of which can be resumed or deleted; right-click one to copy it.
BootChecks.StopBisectionButton.Tooltip: Stops after the current run, puts your load order back and saves the session for later.
BootChecks.Title: Boot Checks
BootChecks.WasOnCheckBox.Tooltip: Was on for the run you are about to record below.
BugReport.CopyBBCodeButton.Tooltip: Copies the report in the markup a Nexus mod page comment reads.
BugReport.CopyMarkdownButton.Tooltip: Copies the report in the markup a GitHub issue reads.

BugReport.Expander.Blurb: BEM writes it, you post it. It states what happened on this machine, what your setup is, and which launches showed it. It never tells the author how to fix anything, and it goes nowhere until you copy or save it yourself.
BugReport.Expander.Tooltip: Writes a report you can post on the mod's page. BEM never sends it anywhere.
BugReport.ListModsButton.Tooltip: Reads your load order and lists every mod a report could be about, strongest evidence first.
BugReport.PreviewText.Tooltip: Read this before you post it. Select any part of it to copy it.
BugReport.QualityText.Tooltip: How strong this report is, what it carries, and what one more launch would add.
BugReport.SaveButton.Tooltip: Writes the report to a file you choose, as Markdown or as BBCode.
BugReport.ShowBBCodeCheckBox.Tooltip: Switches the preview between the two markups. Both say exactly the same thing.
BugReport.SubjectsList.Tooltip: Pick the mod the report is about.
BugReport.TitleText.Tooltip: The title to put on a GitHub issue. Select it to copy it.

Diagnostics.ButrPrivacyBlurb: What goes is the game version, the exception and its call stack, the modules that were installed, and the ones BEM blames for this crash. What never goes is a file path, your Windows user name, your machine name, any key, and any identifier that would join two of your reports together. The report is anonymous: no account and no sign-in. The same crash is never sent twice from this machine, and no more than ten go in a day.
Diagnostics.ButrScoringBlurb: BUTR scores a module by counting the crash reports it appears in, so a crash report is the only thing the service accepts: there is no endpoint for a run that went well. BEM reads those scores on the Settings page and, until you switch this on, has never given anything back to them.
Diagnostics.ButrUntestedBlurb: BEM has never called BUTR's upload endpoint, so it cannot promise the endpoint still answers. If it refuses or cannot be reached, the line under the buttons says exactly that and nothing is recorded as contributed.

Environment.FetchFresh.Dialog.Body.one: BEM asks Nexus once for everything published recently, then once more for each of your {0} checkable mod that the answer says has a new file. That is one request plus however many changed, not one per mod.{1}Nexus allows a limited number of requests per hour and per day, and that allowance is shared with any other mod manager signed in as you. BEM stops with headroom to spare rather than leaving your downloads to fail. The Settings page shows what is left.

Environment.FindModPages.Dialog.Body: BEM has no Nexus mod page for {0} of your modules. It asks Nexus to identify any archive it still has on disk by that file's own hash, which is one request per archive and is proof rather than a resemblance, and then reads BUTR's public index for whatever is left, which costs nothing.{1}Nothing the index suggests is recorded until you have looked at it. Nexus allows a limited number of requests per hour and per day, shared with any other mod manager signed in as you.

Install.CoverageDetailExpander.ButrNote: Search BUTR's index: the BUTR community site downloads every Bannerlord mod on Nexus and reads the module id out of it, so its index can name the page a module came from with no archive left on disk. Reading it signs in to BUTR with your stored Nexus key, which is what BUTR's own tools do. Nexus is then asked what each candidate page is called, so a choice between two mod ids is a choice between two names rather than two numbers, and a page already asked about costs nothing to ask again. Nothing found is recorded until you tick it, and a matching name never ticks anything by itself.
Install.CoverageDetailExpander.DeletedAr: Read deleted archive names: an installed and deleted archive still carries its mod id in its name until the Recycle Bin is emptied. Only names are read. No file is opened, restored, moved, copied or deleted, a name is used only when it lands on exactly one installed module, and nothing recovered this way replaces what BEM recorded at install.
Install.CoverageDetailExpander.HashNote: Identify by file hash: BEM hashes every archive it installs, whether it came from a link or was downloaded by hand. Nexus publishes one lookup keyed on what a file contains, so that hash asks it outright which mod page, which file and which version you have. That is the only comparison that can say out of date for certain. It needs you signed in to Nexus.
Install.CoverageDetailExpander.Header.To: Open this to read where each count above was measured.
Install.CoverageDetailExpander.InstallLo: Read BEM's own install log: BEM writes down every archive it installs and the folder each module inside it lands in, so a module installed before BEM began keeping that record can still be traced back to the archive it came from. This runs on its own because it reads nothing but BEM's own files and asks Nexus nothing. A folder that is no longer installed is skipped, and a module two archives claim for different mod pages gets neither.
Install.CoverageDetailExpander.SourceNot: Nexus can only be asked about a module BEM has a mod id for. The module's own SubModule.xml is the best source; where it says nothing, BEM falls back on the archive it installed the module from. Nearly every mod on your install does have a mod id, so a module counted here is one BEM has not found the id for rather than one that has none, and it is reported as not checked rather than guessed at.

Install.ModuleFilesBlurb: An archive of loose files with no module in it replaces files inside modules you already have. BEM shows what would change before writing, merges parseable XML entry by entry so nothing the installed file has is lost, and keeps a copy of the file that was there. Pick a file to put one back, or restore every replaced file at once. What is there now goes to the Recycle Bin either way, so a restore can be undone. Steam may put its own copy back over a file inside an official module.
Install.ModuleFoldersBlurb: Installing a mod you already have replaces its whole folder in Modules. The folder that was there is moved into BEM's quarantine folder instead of being deleted, so the version you had is still on disk. With "Replace the whole module folder on install" off in Settings, the new files are written into the folder where it stands and a copy of it is taken into the same quarantine first, so either way the version you had is still on disk. Restoring one moves the folder that is installed now into the same quarantine first, so nothing is overwritten either way.
Install.ModuleFoldersOffNote: Off means the existing folder is deleted outright, or written over in place, with no copy kept, and nothing can put it back.

Install.PlatformDetectionBlurb: BEM reads which platform your install runs from the bin folder it actually has: Win64_Shipping_Client for Steam, GOG and Epic, or Gaming.Desktop.x64_Shipping_Client for Xbox Game Pass PC. If it cannot tell, or the install somehow has both, nothing is treated as the wrong platform and every module keeps everything it shipped.
Install.PlatformSpareBlurb: A folder is only spare when the same module also ships the one your install loads. A module whose only binaries are for the other platform is never moved out, because that would leave it installed and inert. Copy them across instead: the files are put where your game looks and the originals stay where they are. Only bin\Win64_Shipping_Client and bin\Gaming.Desktop.x64_Shipping_Client are ever touched, so an editor build such as Win64_Shipping_wEditor is left alone. Nothing is deleted: folders move to a quarantine folder and can be restored.

Overlaps.CollisionsSection.Description: Two mods on one method is normal. Harmony runs postfixes and finalizers one after another by design, so only the ones where they compete for the same body are listed first, and each says why.
Overlaps.CollisionsSection.Tooltip: Harmony patches from different mods landing on the same method.

Overlaps.MergeFaultsSection.Blurb: The game keys each dataset's schema on where an element sits, not on what it is called, and it looks that key up without checking. A mod that puts a valid element under the wrong parent, or a stylesheet that writes one, loads fine on its own and kills the merge the moment a second mod edits the same entry. The game boots and then dies on Start a new campaign. BEM runs the same merge here and names what it hits.
Overlaps.MergeFaultsSection.Tooltip: Places the game's own XML merge throws instead of finishing.

Overlaps.OverridingBaseGameHeading.Descr: Replacing base game data is how a mod rebalances the game, so these are here to show what each one changes rather than because anything is wrong. There is nothing to fix and no button: turn the mod off if you do not want its version.
Overlaps.OverridingBaseGameHeading.Toolt: How each mod rebalances the base game, listed rather than flagged.
Overlaps.OverridingEachOtherHeading.Desc: Each row is one attribute of one kind of element, with every entry the mods disagree about listed inside it. The mod that loads last keeps its value and the earlier ones are discarded with nothing logged. Where nothing declares an order, the winner is only where the two happened to sort, so Make X win reorders them on the Play tab and changes it.
Overlaps.OverridingEachOtherHeading.Tool: Two mods setting one attribute differently, where load order alone decides the winner.
Overlaps.RegistryHeading.Tooltip: How old the captured Harmony snapshot is, and whether it matches your load order.
Overlaps.ShowOnPlayMenuItem: Show this module on the Play tab
Overlaps.ShowOnPlayMenuItem.Tooltip: Jumps to Play with this module picked out in the load order.
Overlaps.Title: Mod Overlaps
Overlaps.TransformsHeading.Description: Some mods edit a dataset with an XSLT stylesheet instead of shipping entries. BEM runs each one against its own in-memory copy of the merged document, with script and external references switched off, and counts the result above. Your files are only ever read.
Overlaps.TransformsHeading.Tooltip: Stylesheets a mod uses to edit a dataset instead of shipping entries.
Overlaps.XmlOverlapRow.Tooltip: Open this to read every value the game throws away here.
Overlaps.XmlOverlapsSection.Blurb: Mods add and rebalance items, troops, cultures and text by shipping XML the game merges together, attribute by attribute. Two mods that edit different parts of the same entry both get their way; a value is lost only where they set the same attribute to different values, and the loser is discarded with nothing written anywhere. BEM runs the game's own merge to work out which ones those are.
Overlaps.XmlOverlapsSection.Tooltip: Values two mods set differently, where only the later one survives.

Settings.ButrContributeSection.Blurb: A score is a count of crash reports, so the only way to add to one is to send a crash report. That sits with the crashes, on the Crash Reports page. It is off until you turn it on there, it shows you the whole report before anything is sent, and nothing goes until you press send.

Settings.ButrContribution.NoInstall: The game install could not be found, so no crash report could be read.
Settings.ButrContribution.NoModules: No modules could be scanned, so there is nothing to file a crash report against.

Settings.ButrContribution.OnNote: Contributing is on. Nothing is sent until you prepare a crash report and press send.
Settings.ButrContribution.PrepareFailed: The crash report could not be prepared, so nothing was sent.

Settings.ButrContribution.ReportRead: Read the newest crash report, written {0}.

Settings.ButrScore.DetailWithRecommendat: Compatibility {0} percent. The community's best result on this game version is {1} at {2} percent.
Settings.ButrScoresSection.Blurb: BUTR runs a community service that scores how often each module version appears in crash reports for a given game version. BEM can ask it about your modules and show what it says. The request is anonymous: no account, no key, nothing that identifies you. What leaves your machine is the list of module ids and versions plus your game version.
Settings.ButrScoresSection.Disclaimer: A score is advice and nothing more. It never changes your load order, never changes a sort and never changes how severely BEM treats anything. A module the service has no data for is listed as having no data, which says nothing about whether it works.
Settings.CancelButrFetchButton.Tooltip: Stops the score request that is running; whatever already came back stays on screen.
Settings.CancelNexusSignInButton.Tooltip: Stops the sign-in that is waiting on your browser and leaves any key you already stored untouched.
Settings.CancelNexusUpdateCheckButton.To: Stops the update check that is running; whatever it already found stays on screen.
Settings.CheckBemUpdateButton.Tooltip: Asks BEM's Nexus page for its published version and compares it against this build; no key is needed.
Settings.CheckNexusApiKeyButton.Tooltip: Asks Nexus whether the stored key is valid and shows the answer below; nothing else about your account is read.
Settings.CheckNexusUpdatesNowButton.Tool: Asks Nexus now which of your installed mods had files uploaded in the chosen period and lists what it found.
Settings.CrashHandlingSection.DisabledOp: Two more are deliberately left out because they do nothing in the installed BLSE build. Disable Binary Compatibility Check has no code reading it at all, and LauncherEx labels it DISABLED! itself. Fix Common Issues is read but its check exits before it runs, so no one has ever received that fix; the only thing it looks for is a stray 0Harmony.dll in bin\Win64_Shipping_Client. Showing either as a working toggle here would be a lie.
Settings.CrashHandlingSection.LauncherEx: BLSE's other options are not shown here. Six of them only change the BLSE LauncherEx window, which BEM replaces: window size, hiding the splash image, the compact module list, DPI scaling, beta sorting and automatic update checks. Two more are buttons that restore the engine and game option backups LauncherEx takes when you edit those settings through it, which BEM does not edit. Set all of those in LauncherEx if you want them.
Settings.DeleteArchivesCheckBox.Tooltip: On, the archive file is deleted from your archives folder once its mod has installed successfully. Off, it stays where it is and can be installed again.
Settings.DiagnosticsSection.Blurb: Logs are written here and are the first thing to check when something goes wrong.
Settings.DisableAutoGenExceptionsCheckBo: Stop catching exceptions from auto-generated methods

Sends /disableautogenexceptions. Leave it off unless BLSE keeps interrupting you with exception popups. Note BLSE LauncherEx ships with this turned on, so coming from LauncherEx you may see popups here that you did not see there.
Settings.EnableButrScoresCheckBox: Ask BUTR for community compatibility scores
Settings.EnableButrScoresCheckBox.Toolti: On, BEM may ask BUTR's anonymous service how often each of your module versions appears in crash reports. What leaves this machine is the module ids, their versions and your game version, and a score never changes anything BEM does.
Settings.EnableNexusUpdateCheckCheckBox: Check installed mods for new files on Nexus
On, BEM may ask Nexus which of your installed mods have had new files uploaded and list them here. It reports only: nothing is downloaded, installed or reordered, and nothing is asked until you sign in and press Check Now.
Settings.EnableNxmHandlerCheckBox: Let BEM handle Nexus Mod Manager links
Settings.EnableNxmHandlerCheckBox.Toolti: On, Windows opens Nexus mod manager links with BEM and a Bannerlord download is saved to your archives folder. Off, they go back to whichever program held them before.
Settings.ExtraLaunchArguments.Tooltip: Extra command-line arguments passed to the game on every launch, added after the ones BEM builds itself. Leave it empty unless you know you need one.
Settings.FetchButrScoresButton.Tooltip: Asks BUTR now for a compatibility score for each installed module on your game version and lists what came back.
Settings.FoldersSection.Blurb: The two folders the Library page works with, and the only paths BEM needs to know.
Settings.GameInstallFolder.Tooltip: Where Bannerlord itself is installed. BEM reads modules, saves and crash reports from here.
Settings.InstallSelectedOnlyCheckBox.Too: On, Install All installs only the archives you ticked on the Library page. Off, it installs every archive that was detected.
Settings.InstallSevenZipOnDemandCheckBox: Install 7-Zip for me when a mod needs it

Off by default: it installs a third-party program on your machine. Nothing is installed until a .7z or .rar actually needs it, and what happened is written to the log and shown with the install result.
Off, a .7z or .rar install stops and tells you where to get 7-Zip. On, BEM runs the command below the first time one needs it and then carries on with the install.
Settings.KeepCrashHandlerUnderDebuggerCh: Keep the BLSE crash handler on when a debugger is attached
Sends /enablecrashhandlerwhendebuggerisattached. Off, BLSE steps aside so your debugger sees the exception first. Only useful if you attach a debugger to the game.
Settings.KeepDividersAnchoredCheckBox: Keep sections with their modules when Auto-Sorting
Settings.KeepDividersAnchoredCheckBox.To: Off, Auto-Sort moves every section to the bottom of the list, since it does not know what your grouping means. On, each section stays with the module it was sitting above, wherever Auto-Sort moves that module to.
Settings.KeepVanillaCrashHandlerCheckBox: Sends /enablevanillacrashhandler. Off, BLSE adds no_watchdog and reports crashes itself. On, TaleWorlds' Watchdog stays alive instead.
Settings.Language.RestartBody: BEM restarts to finish changing the language, so nothing is left half translated. Restart now?
Settings.Language.RestartFailed: BEM could not restart itself. Close it and open it again to finish changing the language.
Settings.Language.Tooltip: Choose the language BEM displays, which restarts the app.
Settings.LaunchTargetCombo.Tooltip: Which program Play starts the game through, such as BLSE or the game's own launcher. Only targets found on this machine are listed.
Settings.MinimizeOnLaunchCheckBox.Toolti: On, the BEM window minimizes as soon as the game starts and keeps running behind it. Off, it stays where it is.
Settings.ModSettingsButton.Tooltip: Archives, restores and shares each mod's settings folder.
Settings.ModuleRowDensityCombo.Tooltip: How tall each module row is on the Play page. More compact rows put more modules on screen.
Settings.NetworkFeaturesExpander.Blurb: Everything else in BEM works with no network at all. The features below are the only ones that reach the internet, and each can be switched off here. Nothing is ever downloaded or installed for you.
Settings.NetworkFeaturesExpander.Tooltip: Opens every setting that reaches the internet: Nexus update checking, Nexus mod manager links, and the BUTR compatibility scores. Each one is switched on and off on its own.
Settings.Nexus.AcceptableUsePolicyLabel: the Nexus API acceptable use policy
Opens the Nexus acceptable use policy for their API in your browser, which is the agreement your key is issued under.
Settings.NexusApiKeyLabel.Blurb: The key Nexus sends when you sign in is encrypted with Windows DPAPI for your Windows account and stored only on this machine: it is sent to nexusmods.com and nowhere else, and it is never written to a log, a report or a shared settings bundle.
Settings.NexusPeriodCombo.Tooltip: How far back the check looks for files uploaded to Nexus; a longer period returns more mods and spends more of your request quota.
Settings.NexusQuota.Note: This quota is shared with any other mod manager signed in as you.
Settings.NexusQuota.RemainingUnknown: an unknown number of requests left
Settings.NexusQuota.Unknown: Nexus request quota is not known yet.
Settings.NexusSignInLabel.Blurb: Sign in and approve BEM once in your browser, and Nexus sends the key straight back. Nothing else about your Nexus account is read.
Settings.NexusSso.UnavailableNote: Signing in with Nexus is not enabled yet. It needs an application identifier that Nexus issues only after approving the application, and BEM has not been issued one.
Settings.NexusSsoButton.Tooltip: Opens your browser to approve BEM, then stores the key Nexus sends back.
Settings.NexusSsoButton.Tooltip.Unavaila: Work in progress: waiting on the NexusMods.com Team to approve BEM's application identifier.
Settings.NexusUpdateCheckSection.Blurb: BEM can ask Nexus which Bannerlord mods have had new files uploaded recently, and tell you which of yours are among them. It is information only: BEM never downloads a mod, never installs one and never changes your load order because of it. It needs you signed in to Nexus, and it does nothing at all until you are.
Settings.NexusUpdateRow.OpenOnNexusButto: Opens this mod's own Nexus page in your browser.
Settings.Nxm.ArchivesFolder.None: No archives folder is set, so there is nowhere to save a Bannerlord download. Set one in Settings.
Settings.Nxm.PreviousHandler.None: No other program was holding Nexus links when BEM took them, so there is nothing to pass anything on to.
Settings.Nxm.PreviousHandler.Some: Links that are not Bannerlord downloads are passed to {0}
Settings.NxmLinksSection.Blurb: With this on, clicking Mod Manager Download on a Bannerlord mod page sends the download to BEM, which saves the archive into your archives folder ready to install. Only one program at a time can hold these links on Windows. A link for any other game, a collection, or a Nexus sign-in goes straight to whichever program held them before BEM, without BEM opening. Turning this off hands them back.
Settings.NxmLinksSection.VortexNote: Vortex rewrites this registration every time Vortex starts, so BEM re-asserts it every time BEM starts. To stop the two swapping it back and forth, turn off Handle Nexus Links in Vortex under Settings, Downloads.
Settings.OpenBemNexusPageButton.Tooltip: Opens BEM's own Nexus Mods page in your browser, where a newer version is downloaded like any other release.
Settings.OpenCrashReportsButton.Tooltip: Opens the page where a crash report can be contributed to BUTR.
Settings.OpenLogsFolderButton.Tooltip: Opens the folder holding BEM's own log files in File Explorer, so a log can be read or attached to a bug report.
Settings.OpenUrl.Failure: Could not open {0}. The address is {1}
Settings.PermitManualOverrideCheckBox: Permit manual override of load order rules
Settings.PermitManualOverrideCheckBox.To: Applies to dragging a module by hand and to nothing else. Sorting always satisfies every declared rule whatever this is set to, and an imported load order is always applied exactly as the file has it.
Settings.RefreshToolkitButton.Tooltip: Checks the machine again for each of these programs.

Settings.ReplaceModuleFoldersCheckBox: Replace the whole module folder on install (recommended)
Settings.ReplaceModuleFoldersCheckBox.To: On, the folder that is there is taken out of Modules first and the mod installs into an empty one. Off, the new files are written into the folder where it stands, so files the new version does not include stay behind and can be loaded alongside it. Neither setting loses the version you had: a copy is kept either way, in Replaced module folders on the Library page, under Advanced.
Settings.ReplaceModuleFoldersNote: Off writes the new files over the folder that is there instead of replacing it, which leaves behind any file the new version does not include. A copy of the folder is kept either way.
Settings.SearchArchivesRecursivelyCheckB: On, subfolders of the archives folder are searched too, so an archive filed in a folder of its own is still found. Off, only the folder itself is read.
Settings.ShareGameSettingsCheckBox: Share base game settings across instances
Settings.ShareGameSettingsCheckBox.Toolt: Covers engine_config.txt, BannerlordConfig.txt and BannerlordGameKeys.xml only. Mod settings, load orders and saves are never shared. Turning this off gives an instance that had its own settings those files back, and one that never had any returns to the game's defaults.
Settings.SharedGameSettingsSection.Blurb: Off, every instance uses its own settings file, which is how BEM has always worked. On, one shared set is applied to an instance as it launches, and what you change in game is folded back into the shared set after a run BEM watched to the end, sometimes only at that version's next launch. A setting a newer game version introduced is never pushed onto an older instance, and a keybinding category a mod owns is never created in an instance that does not have that mod.

Watch.Blurb: Records what happened between the game starting and whatever ended it: each module starting and finishing, each mod applying its Harmony patches, and every exception thrown along the way. The line that matters is the last thing that started and never finished.
Watch.CopyTimelineButton.Tooltip: Puts every recorded event, with its details, on the clipboard.
Watch.CostArmedText: While it is armed, every launch BEM starts is watched: Launch on the Play tab as well as the buttons here. A launch you start from Steam or from a shortcut is not, because the companion has to be on the command line's module list to load at all and BEM will not write its own module into your saved load order to change that.
Watch.CostFrameRateText: Its effect on frame rate has not been measured. During loading it writes one line per module and one per mod that patches, which is a few hundred lines. Once you are playing it does nothing per frame except reset a counter, and it writes to disk every five seconds only if something was thrown. Play a session and judge for yourself before trusting it in a long one.
Watch.CostInstallText: It installs BEM's companion module into your game folder and leaves it there until you stop watching, so you can start as many watched launches as you like without installing it again. Launch on the Play tab and the buttons below both start one.
Watch.CostLaunchMethodText: Watching starts the game through BLSE (direct) or Bannerlord.exe, whichever your launch target prefers. A launcher takes no module list on its command line, and BEM will not write its own module into your saved load order to get around that.
Watch.CostOffByDefaultText: Nothing here turns itself on. Watching is off until you press the button, because it puts a module of BEM's into your game folder, and that is a change outside BEM's own files that you should make deliberately.
Watch.CostOverheadText: What it costs to leave armed: roughly 40 to 60 ms on a 20 second load, and one file per mod that patches. Your LauncherData.xml is not written or changed by any of it.
Watch.CostPatchScopeText: It puts a Harmony patch on two of the game's own methods and on Harmony's own patching entry points, and none at all on any mod's code. That distinction is not cosmetic: an earlier version patched 142 mods' own callbacks and caused crashes, because Harmony runs a patched method as a copy with a different identity and obfuscated mods do not survive that.
Watch.LaunchAgainButton.Tooltip: Starts another watched launch without installing the companion again.
Watch.NotWatching: BEM is not watching a play session.
Watch.PatchesExpander.Description: Taken from Harmony at the game's first frame, so it includes patches made from a computed method reference that no scan of the files would find. Press Use this run's patch registry to make this the one BEM reads, then the Diagnostics page answers what is patching a given method and which mods patch the same one.
Watch.PatchesExpander.Tooltip: How many methods each mod patched, taken from Harmony itself.
Watch.RecordedButGone: BEM recorded a watch session but its companion is no longer in the game folder, so nothing is being watched. Stop watching to clear this.
Watch.Refuse.Message: {0} is not the version resting at the machine's Bannerlord folders, so BEM cannot keep this version's data isolated for a whole watched session started here; {1} was refused before anything was started. Press 'Start Watching, Do Not Launch' here, then launch from the Play tab, which keeps this version isolated for the whole run.
Watch.RunPicker.Tooltip: Pick which recorded launch to read.
Watch.SaveRegistryButton.Tooltip: Stores what Harmony reported on this launch, so a crash report read later can name what patched a method.
Watch.ShowEveryEventCheckBox.Tooltip: Shows all of it, not only the lines worth reading first.
Watch.StartAndLaunchButton: Start watching and launch the game
Watch.StartAndLaunchButton.Tooltip: Installs the companion and starts the game; every launch BEM starts is watched until you stop.
Watch.StopButton: Stop watching and remove the companion
Watch.StopButton.Tooltip: Takes the companion out of your game folder and out of your saved load order, and keeps everything already recorded.
Watch.Timeline.Copy.Failure: Could not copy: another program is holding the clipboard.
Watch.Timeline.Copy.Success: Copied the whole timeline to the clipboard.
Watch.Title: Watch a Play Session
Watch.TraceFrequencyText: It is written every few seconds, so a session that ends in a hard crash still leaves what was thrown just before it. The same runs are readable on the Diagnostics page under first-chance exceptions.
Watch.TraceScopeText: The trace is only half of it. BEM also copies what the game, ButterLib and each mod write during every run, because the game deletes its own crash folder seconds after sending it. Those copies are read under Runs BEM captured, on the Boot Checks page, and they are there whether or not you were watching.
